drug_indication: Metastatic RAS G12D Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
catalyst_text: Began Phase 3 trial in G12D metastatic PDAC
detailed_catalyst_text: The company began treating patients in RASolute 305, a global, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial of zoldonrasib plus chemotherapy as first-line therapy for metastatic RAS G12D pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The study compares the combination against placebo plus chemotherapy with primary endpoints of progression-free survival and overall survival, aiming to improve outcomes in this high-need population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Revolution Medicines... today announced that it has begun treating patients in RASolute 305, a global, randomized Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating zoldonrasib in combination with standard of care chemotherapy as a first line treatment in patients with metastatic RAS G12D pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). RASolute 305 (NCT07621718) is a global, randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial evaluating zoldonrasib plus investigator’s choice of standard of care chemotherapy compared with placebo plus investigator’s choice of chemotherapy in patients with previously untreated metastatic RAS G12D PDAC. The primary endpoints are progression-free survival and overall survival.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 3 results meeting primary endpoints
detailed_catalyst_text: Detailed results from a global, randomized Phase 3 trial in previously treated metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma showed significant overall survival and progression-free survival benefits versus standard chemotherapy. The study met all primary and key secondary endpoints and demonstrated a manageable safety profile with improved patient-reported outcomes. These data indicate a clinically meaningful benefit over chemotherapy for this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Revolution Medicines, Inc. ... today announced detailed results from the global, randomized Phase 3 RASolute 302 clinical trial evaluating daraxonrasib, an oral RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor, in patients with previously treated metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). In the randomized Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial, once-daily oral daraxonrasib demonstrated unprecedented improvements in overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) compared to standard of care cytotoxic chemotherapy in patients with previously treated metastatic PDAC, with or without an identified tumor RAS mutation. All primary and key secondary endpoints of the trial were met. The results will be presented during a late-breaking Plenary Session (LBA5) at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting at 3:21 p.m. CDT today and were published today in The New England Journal of Medicine.

drug_indication: KRAS G12D Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1 results in G12D NSCLC
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 1 results from the RMC-9805-001 study in previously treated KRAS G12D non-small cell lung cancer were presented, showing encouraging efficacy and safety. Among eligible patients, confirmed objective response rate was 52% and disease control rate was 93%, with mostly Grade 1 adverse events and no Grade 4 or 5 events. These findings indicate meaningful antitumor activity with a manageable safety profile in this molecular subset.
catalyst_text_evidence: Revolution Medicines, Inc. (NASDAQ:RVMD)... today announced updated Phase 1 (RMC-9805-001) clinical data for zoldonrasib, an oral RAS(ON) G12D-selective inhibitor, in patients with previously treated KRAS G12D non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The data to be presented at the AACR Annual Meeting are as of a 2025-12-01 data cutoff, and included 40 patients with KRAS G12D NSCLC treated with zoldonrasib 1200 mg once daily, the recommended Phase 2 dose, and who were evaluable for safety. Zoldonrasib was generally well tolerated and demonstrated a safety profile consistent with previously reported findings. Among this subset of patients (n=27), the confirmed objective response rate was 52% (confidence interval (CI): 32, 71) and the disease control rate was 93% (CI: 76, 99). Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 11.1 months (95% CI: 5.3, not estimable), with an estimated 12-month PFS rate of 48% (95% CI: 27, 66).

catalyst_text: Trial met primary and key secondary endpoints
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported positive topline results from the global, randomized Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial in previously treated metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The study met all primary and key secondary endpoints and showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in progression-free and overall survival versus chemotherapy, including median OS of 13.2 vs 6.7 months (HR 0.40).
catalyst_text_evidence: Trial met all primary and key secondary endpoints, including progression-free survival and overall survival Company intends to include these data in a future New Drug Application submission to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and to other global regulatory authorities. REDWOOD CITY, Calif., 2026-04-13 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Revolution Medicines, a late-stage clinical oncology company developing targeted therapies for patients with RAS-addicted cancers, today announced positive topline results from its global, randomized, controlled Phase 3 RASolute 302 clinical trial evaluating daraxonrasib in patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) who had been previously treated. Daraxonrasib taken orally once daily demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) compared with standard of care cytotoxic chemotherapy delivered intravenously. In the overall (intent-to-treat) study population, daraxonrasib demonstrated a median OS of 13.2 months versus 6.7 months for chemotherapy, with a hazard ratio of 0.40 (p < 0.0001). Based on the results from this first interim analysis, all PFS and OS endpoint results are considered final.

catalyst_text: Began treating patients in global Phase 3 trial
detailed_catalyst_text: The company initiated patient dosing in RASolute 303, a global Phase 3 study testing daraxonrasib alone and with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel in first-line metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. This marks the start of a registrational trial in this population, with primary endpoints of progression-free and overall survival.
catalyst_text_evidence: REDWOOD CITY, Calif., 2026-04-02 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Revolution Medicines, a late-stage clinical oncology company developing targeted therapies for patients with RAS-addicted cancers, today announced that it has begun treating patients in RASolute 303, a global Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating daraxonrasib as monotherapy and in combination with chemotherapy in patients with previously untreated metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), a disease predominantly driven by oncogenic RAS variants. RASolute 303 (NCT07491445) is a global, randomized, open-label Phase 3 trial evaluating daraxonrasib as monotherapy or in combination with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel versus standard-of-care gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel in patients with previously untreated metastatic PDAC.

catalyst_text: First patient dosed in phase 1 clinical trial
detailed_catalyst_text: The company reported dosing the first patient in a first-in-human, open-label study of a RAS(ON) G12V-selective inhibitor. The trial enrolls patients with RAS G12V–mutated solid tumors, including pancreatic, colorectal, and non–small cell lung cancers. This marks clinical initiation of a targeted therapy for a common RAS mutation with high unmet need.
catalyst_text_evidence: Revolution Medicines, a late-stage clinical oncology company developing targeted therapies for patients with RAS-addicted cancers, today announced the first patient was dosed in its first-in-human clinical trial evaluating RMC-5127, a RAS(ON) G12V-selective inhibitor. The first-in-human trial, RMC-5127-001 [NCT07349537], is an open-label trial evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary antitumor activity of RMC-5127 as both a monotherapy and in combination settings. The trial will enroll patients with RAS G12V–mutated solid tumors, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), colorectal cancer (CRC), and non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), who have progressed on or are intolerant to prior standard therapies, including targeted treatments.

drug_indication: KRAS G12D-mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
catalyst_text: Received FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation for indication
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for a KRAS G12D-mutated NSCLC population previously treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy and platinum chemotherapy. The designation, based on Phase 1 monotherapy data, recognizes substantial unmet need and may expedite development and review.
catalyst_text_evidence: Revolution Medicines, Inc. ... announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to zoldonrasib, a RAS(ON) G12D-selective inhibitor, for the treatment of adult patients with KRAS G12D-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who have been previously treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy. The Breakthrough Therapy Designation is based on data from the monotherapy cohort of the Phase 1 RMC-9805-001 clinical trial evaluating zoldonrasib in patients with advanced KRAS G12D solid tumors.

catalyst_text: First patient randomized in Phase 3 PDAC trial
detailed_catalyst_text: The first patient was randomized in RASolute 304, a global Phase 3 study in resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma after surgery and perioperative chemotherapy. The trial assesses improvement in disease-free survival versus observation, marking advancement of the program into a pivotal setting.
catalyst_text_evidence: Revolution Medicines, a late-stage clinical oncology company developing targeted therapies for patients with RAS-addicted cancers, today announced the first patient has been randomized in the RASolute 304 trial. RASolute 304 is a global, open-label, Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of daraxonrasib, a RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor, in patients with resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) who have received surgery and chemotherapy. The trial will assess whether daraxonrasib can improve disease-free survival compared to observation.
